cells.tense: The fire is caught here now, and the people around you can feel it
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Do the next piece of the shared work — the piece after the one you just finished — and don't stop to check whether anything came back.
cells.core:
Something lit up in the shared thing you're part of — a practice, a room, a way of doing it that other people hold too — and nobody had to hand it to you. You're in the middle of it, not at the edge. That's why you can tell a real morning from a stalling one: the direction is picked, the repetitions are yours, and the fire has something to eat.

Since you already chose it, don't wait for the light to come back to prove it left. Choose one thread you've been holding with the others and do the next piece of it, whatever they send back or don't. A sign only arrives once it's had time to be earned. Keep at the version you chose a while longer, and treat the keeping as the work itself.
cells.sheetLine: The fire is already going and it's yours.
cells.verb: lighting up before there is anywhere to point it
cells.place: where a shared meaning gets carried from one person to the next

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of the thing is being built here before today's has burned
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Put everything you've already built for the shared thing on one table at its true size, and add nothing to it.
cells.core:
When this much is happening at once, the future of the place gets built before any of it exists. The language is finished in your head, the tradition is already carrying, the next gathering is furnished — and it's all out ahead of what's actually here. The people who'd hold it with you can't see the whole of it, because you keep the whole of it in advance. An advance picture isn't the same as the thing.

Lay out what's really been made so far — every piece, at its true size — and look at the lot before adding one more. Then start one thing in front of someone, on the strength of what exists and not what's coming. Let them watch it be made instead of being shown it finished. When nothing's hidden, they can hold it alongside you, and the spark stops having to carry tomorrow.

cells.tense: The fire was lit a long time ago and the shared place has gone quiet since
cells.act: take in the whole rainbow of what you feel
cells.ask: Choose one old piece of the tradition — a song, a dish, the words — and spend an evening inside it, taking in whatever arrives, the warm and the sour together.
cells.core:
In the shared places — the family thing, the practice a group of you kept, the language you grew up inside — you're not really arriving. Something lit up once, and you've carried the shape of it since without carrying the fire. You can still do the moves. The old ways are in your hands and nothing in you is landing on them.

Begin with the old things themselves, not with yourself. Take one from the tradition — a song, a dish, a set of words — and let what it holds come up all the way: the warm and the sour at once, in whatever form it shows, until you have the whole of it. Nothing gets crossed out. Stop when the evening ends. Feeling returns through the things that carry it, not through being asked for directly.

cells.tense: The spark keeps arriving here, and your version says the air does it
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Go through a finished piece of the shared thing — the passage, the recipe, the tune — as it stands, all the way through, changing none of it.
cells.core:
Something keeps getting lit in the shared work, and you keep crediting the atmosphere or the group's energy. The version of you that ignores the fire is the one answering questions about it. When someone says the place feels alive now, you change the subject or give the crowd the credit, and the flame that started it goes unnamed.

Before the place was lively, it was one person starting something. So handle a finished piece as the maker, not as its cleaner. Take what you already built — the passage, the recipe, the tune — and use it as it stands, at its real size, without improving it. Then notice whose work it was. Naming that doesn't cost the place anything. The light gets to be a person's, and starting stays something you do rather than something that happens to a room.
cells.sheetLine: The light keeps coming, and you credit the atmosphere.

attempts.check: The one unsupported claim is that the too-little person still shows up at the shared thing while feeling nothing in it — the record says only that the capacity is under-expressed at Culture, not that the person is present at all, so I have kept 'showing up' out of the cell and left the absence of arrival. A reader could reasonably say 'I walked away from that years ago, I'm not lurking at any door' — the ask survives that because it works on any gathering, close or small, done before leaving, so a person returned or holding back is still served. The sentence that serves me more than them would be 'there is something waiting in you' — it makes the card sound like a promise, so I have not used it.
